scenes.heading: Knowing when to bring on help and how to structure a small team

sents.d: Knowing when to bring on help and how to structure a small team
Growth usually requires delegating repeatable tasks before delegating strategy.
The clearest signal it's time to hire is having a specific, repeatable task — content scheduling, basic graphic creation, comment moderation — that's clearly defined enough to document and hand off.

Starting with a part-time contractor for a narrow task (e.g. scheduling and basic community management) is lower-risk than hiring a full-time employee to handle an undefined range of responsibilities.

Keeping strategy and client relationships with yourself initially, while delegating execution tasks, allows you to grow capacity without losing the client trust that's often tied specifically to you as the strategist.

take: Delegate clearly defined tasks first; keep the strategy yourself.
